AWARDHONOR.NAME: ASME Robbert E. Abbott Award
AWARDHONOR.DESC: The ASME Robert E. Abbott Award is one of the most prestigious honors conferred by the ASME Design Engineering Division, recognizing sustained and foundational contributions that have significantly advanced the field of design engineering. The scope of the award encompasses long-term excellence in research, education, and professional service, with emphasis on impact that shapes both engineering theory and practice. Recipients are individuals whose work has influenced design methodologies, analytical and computational tools, experimental approaches, and the broader engineering community over many years. Selection is made through rigorous peer review within ASME, making the award a strong marker of professional distinction and leadership. As such, the Robert E. Abbott Award carries substantial weight within the mechanical and design engineering communities and represents recognition by peers of enduring technical impact, scholarly excellence, and exceptional service to the profession.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Equipment: MRI: Track 1 Acquisition of Polytec MSA-600 Micro System Analyzer for Biomedical Engineering
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: Federal
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Requested Instrument: Polytec MSA-600-X/U Micro System Analyzer ($695,790), state-of-the-art instrument crucial for biomedical engineering research and education the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). The location of the instrument is the BIO-MEMS Laboratory (Director Caruntu). Servingover 34,000 students, UTRGV is a non-PhD-granting, minority-serving institution with a predominantly Hispanic student body (92%). The university aims to become an emerging research institution and establish a strong biomedical engineering community. This advanced equipment is crucial to preparing students in engineering, science, and medicine by providing hands-on research experiences that can lead to graduate studies, academic roles, or leadership positions in industry. UTRGV is experiencing rapid growth, with increasing student enrollment and the hiring of new faculty. A recently formed Biomedical Engineering(BME) Cluster for research and education includes eight faculty members, four of whom were hired within the past two years. Supporting faculty research development depends on access to cutting-edge infrastructure like the requested analyzer. Securing this grant lays a foundation for attracting external funding and fostering multidisciplinary collaborations. The lack of this instrument currently limits research efforts. This proposal is strongly supported by UTRGV administration, aligning with the university’s strategic goal of building a robust biomedical engineering research and education program.

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper investigates the hypothesis that men and women perform differently in virtual environments in terms of balance and coordination during surprise events. It reports on an experiment in human subject balance and coordination using an HTC Vive head-mounted display (HMD) to create a virtual environment. For the experiment, 30 male and 30 female subjects of college age were asked to navigate along a clear path in a virtual world using a controller with their dominant hand and asked to balance a virtual ball on a virtual plate using the other controller in the nondominant hand. The test subjects moved along a clearly marked path, with three surprise obstacles occurring: a large rock landing near the path, an explosion near the path, and a flock of birds coming across the path. Data included six degrees-of-freedom (DOF) trajectories for the head and both hands, as well as data gathered by the computer system on ball location and velocity, plate location and velocity, and ball status. Likert scale questionnaires were answered by the test subjects relative to video game experience, sense of presence, and ease of managing the ball movement. Statistics showed that the male students dropped the ball less frequently at p = 0.0254 and p = 0.0036. In contrast, female students were aware of their performance with correlation levels of 0.632 and 0.588.
